newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to boycott Croatian chess tournament.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to boycott Croatian chess tournament.

text.p: Yugoslavia will not take part in the European men's and women's chess championships in the Croatian city of Pula in May, the Yugoslav chess federation has decided.

"We decided some time ago that this was a political rather than sports issue, and approached Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic," federation president Miodrag Vukovic was quoted as saying by the daily Nasa Borba on Monday.
"Kontic said that although our relations with Croatia were improving, the time was still not right for any Yugoslav athletes or chess players to take part in events in Croatia," said Vukovic.
Croatia fought a war with rump Yugoslavia in 1991 after the breakup of former Yugoslavia. Most sporting contacts since then have had to take place in third countries.
